  \caption{Envelope collapse is tool-bound in PLLuM-8B and not in Bielik-7B.

  \vspace{2pt}
  \begin{minipage}{\linewidth}
  \footnotesize
  Cells report bad envelopes / all steps in that condition, with the share in parentheses;
  a risk ratio is the share in the first row of a block divided by the share in the second.
  A \emph{bad envelope} here is any step carrying a parse error (28, 137 and 141 steps in the
  three runs), the broader of the two definitions used by the source scripts; the narrower one
  counts only flattened envelopes (\texttt{unknown\_action}: 18, 31 and 50 steps).
  The two variables are not fully confounded in the PLLuM run:
  \texttt{convert\_temperature} occurs 14 times outside the third step, and the third step
  occurs 27 times without it. For steps that failed to parse, the tool is read from the
  \texttt{action} field of the raw output, so a step that flattened the envelope by writing
  \texttt{"action": "convert\_temperature"} counts as both ``convert'' and ``bad'' by construction.
  \end{minipage}
